Hi Alex,

Read the sentence before you agree to the link

A useful link needs a reason to be on the page. The reader should be able to follow it and find something relevant.

That’s the idea behind Radar’s optional backlinks network. You choose your topics and review proposals from other businesses.

See the partner’s page and the exact sentence around the proposed link.
See the destination page and why the link fits.
Approve or decline the proposal. Radar re-checks live links weekly.

You can review each proposal yourself. Auto-approval is an optional setting, not the starting point.

Hi Alex,

What happens before an article goes live

You don’t need to arrive with a month of article ideas or a spreadsheet of keywords.

Here’s the workflow once you start your Radar trial:

Radar uses your Business Profile and keyword research to propose topics in Content Calendar.
You approve the topics you want, then review and edit the articles Radar drafts.
Connect a supported publishing destination and schedule the articles you’re ready to put out.

Review comes first by default. Blog autopilot is a separate choice you can make later.

You can start with one article and decide how much of the workflow you want to automate.

Hi Alex,

Find one conversation you can help with

Publishing is one way to get your product in front of people. Joining a useful conversation is another.

The difficult part is finding a discussion where you can help, while there’s still a reason to join it.

Daily Brief looks for relevant conversations across Reddit, X, LinkedIn and Hacker News. It brings the discussion and a suggested reply into Radar so you can review them together.

You decide which conversations are worth your time and make each reply your own before sharing it.

Once you start your trial, try it with one conversation where you have something useful to contribute.

Radar by Thally

Hi Alex,

Your next article might be a page you already have

Before writing something new, it can be useful to look at what people already find on your site.

If your site has Google Search Console data, look for pages that get impressions but few clicks, or queries with an average position around 10–20.

Those are places to investigate. The page may need a clearer title, a fuller answer or an update to an older section.

During your Radar trial, connect Search Console and let the history sync. Performance shows the queries and pages alongside suggested changes you can review and add to Content Calendar.

This guide walks through how to review a page-two opportunity before deciding what to change.

Read the page-two refresh guide

Ekene

Radar by Thally

Hi Alex,

Would an AI assistant recommend your product?

Think of a question someone might ask before discovering your product. Which products would an AI assistant include in its answer?

AI Visibility in Radar checks questions related to your business across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Grok.

Read the response each assistant returned.
See whether your business was mentioned and which pages were cited.
Use a question worth answering as a topic for your Content Calendar.

You can add your own questions, too. A response that hasn’t been collected is shown separately from one where you weren’t mentioned.

Start your trial, then open Performance → AI Visibility to see the answers for yourself.

Try AI Visibility in Radar
